options.salts_anti_aliasing.ssaa.name: Supersampling (SSAA)
options.salts_anti_aliasing.ssaa.tooltip: Renders the world at a higher resolution, then averages it down to your screen to smooth jagged edges and shimmering. 4x renders four times as many pixels (twice the width and twice the height), 9x renders nine times as many, and so on. Higher values look smoother but cost much more performance and GPU memory. Your HUD stays at normal resolution.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.ssaa.warning: Warning: %1$s renders %2$s times as many pixels as your screen. This may heavily impact performance, use large amounts of GPU memory, or exceed your GPU's maximum texture size, in which case SSAA is skipped.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.ssaa.improve: SSAA cannot be turned on or changed while Improved Transparency is on. You can still turn it off.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.filter.name: SSAA Filter
options.salts_anti_aliasing.filter.toolt: How the supersampled image is downscaled to your screen. Area (Exact Box), the default, averages every rendered pixel under each screen pixel: smooth, cheap and free of halos. Bilinear and B-Spline are softer. Mitchell-Netravali balances blur and ringing. Catmull-Rom, Bicubic and the Lanczos filters are progressively sharper and can add faint halos around high-contrast edges. The wider filters (Bicubic, Lanczos) cost noticeably more at high SSAA levels. Box and Nearest Neighbor are mainly for comparison; Nearest Neighbor does no anti-aliasing. Only applies while SSAA is on.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.sharpness.to: Averaging many pixels into one removes jagged edges but also softens fine detail slightly. This adds a gentle, edge-aware sharpen to the result to win some of that back. Low is meant to roughly match the crispness of rendering without SSAA; Medium and High go beyond it and can add faint halos around high-contrast edges. Only applies while SSAA is on.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.antilag.name: AMD Anti-Lag
options.salts_anti_aliasing.antilag.tool: Asks your AMD graphics driver (VK_AMD_anti_lag) to stop the CPU running ahead of the GPU, which shortens the delay between your input and the picture on screen. It is separate from SSAA and works with it on or off, and it takes effect immediately. It only does something when Minecraft renders with Vulkan on an AMD GPU whose driver supports it.
options.salts_anti_aliasing.antilag.stat: Not active: Minecraft's Vulkan renderer was not detected.
